chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muskān, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The major sins are seven: killing the believer deliberately, slandering the chaste woman, fleeing from the battlefield, reverting to desert life after the hijrah, consuming the wealth of the orphan unjustly, consuming usury after the clarification, and everything for which Allah has made the Fire obligatory.

key_terms.التَّعَرُّبُ بَعْدَ الْهِجْرَةِ: returning to uncultured desert life after migration, implying religious regression
key_terms.الرِّبَا: usury, the unlawful increase in financial dealings
key_terms.النَّارَ: the Fire, meaning divine punishment in the Hereafter
key_terms.الْفِرَارُ مِنَ الزَّحْفِ: fleeing from the battlefield during combat
key_terms.الْكَبَائِرُ: the major sins, meaning the gravest acts of disobedience
key_terms.قَتْلُ الْمُؤْمِنِ: killing a believer, referring to unlawful taking of a believer's life
key_terms.قَذْفُ الْمُحْصَنَةِ: slandering a chaste woman with false accusation
key_terms.مَالِ الْيَتِيمِ: the property of the orphan, whose wrongful consumption is forbidden

ai.seo_question: What are the major sins mentioned by Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith identifies major sins and highlights acts that bring severe divine punishment. It emphasizes the sanctity of life, honor, social responsibility, and financial justice, while warning that any deed for which Allah has obligated the Fire falls among the gravest sins.
